quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, or angry, they should:

options.text: Let someone else drive.
Pay better attention and drive more carefully.
Drive the same way they normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or upset, let someone else drive. Driving while distracted by strong emotions is never safe.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only check the left side mirror.
Look over your shoulder.
Only check the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. This can happen at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away. When you go faster than 35 mph, tires cannot move the water as well. Your tires lose contact with the road and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: You should signal while turning because it:

options.text: Is required by law.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is unsafe to turn off your signal before finishing the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you intend to do.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light. You should:

options.text: Wait for the light to turn green.
Go through without stopping.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
Carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, you should:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before going down hills. Stay farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. Pump the brakes to slow or stop (unless you have antilock brakes).

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the speed limit based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster. Reduce speed for curves or hills where you cannot see ahead, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: A green traffic signal means you should:

options.text: Stop completely.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Go straight, turn left, or turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight, turn left, or turn right.
questions.explanation: A steady green signal means you may go straight or turn where allowed. Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection when turning.

questions.question: When can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and confirm no trains are coming.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means "go." Turn in the direction the arrow points after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Winter driving is more dangerous because:

options.text: Roads can be affected by ice, snow, and fog.
There are more hours of darkness.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Winter creates many driving hazards. Fog, rain, snow, sleet, ice, and longer dark hours make driving more dangerous. Prepare for these conditions.

questions.question: Vehicles must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only on interstate highways.
Only when driven by a minor.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: The mandatory liability insurance law requires all vehicles to be covered by liability insurance when operated, registered, or maintained. This protects drivers if they are in an accident.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed under normal conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed under normal conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for that road. You may drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
The width of the sidewalk.
Half of a lane width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. You should:

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the driver sees farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would with a car.
Follow one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would with a car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the vehicle ahead stops quickly.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: You are following a small car.
Another driver is tailgating you.
You are driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space ahead and do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Check only the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all other vehicles go first.
Check all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop and check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road has curves ahead.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts drivers to be careful on wet pavement. The road becomes slippery and harder to drive on safely when wet.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start their vehicle without seeing you. Stay alert and ready to react.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on any vehicle or property you hit. Attach it securely to the damaged vehicle or property.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Leave a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Stay three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly and are harder to see. If the rider falls, you need extra distance to avoid them. This is especially important on wet, icy, or gravel roads.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a corner. Yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off moisture and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how can you check your blind spot?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check the areas your mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never block an intersection. Do not enter unless you can get completely across before the light turns red. You can be cited for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are slipperiest during the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and other chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet. Drive with extra caution on slippery roads.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Stay back from motorcycles. They stop faster than other vehicles. You need extra room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Motorcycles are harder to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows and mirrors before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your entire vehicle.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware. Do not stare only ahead. In fog, use low beams, not high beams.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap and shoulder belts. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived before you.
Is across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles proceed through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.
questions.explanation: This sign means yield the right-of-way. Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross before you proceed. Stop if necessary.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers automatically obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Consider the situation and circumstances at every intersection. Yield your legal right-of-way if it helps prevent a collision.
